report_markdown:
The accuracy experiment compares approval-time forecasts with 380 saved actual PyBullet flights; no new ground-truth flights were run. The UAV patrols east, then makes its frozen left turn and flies north. Waiting shifts the turn east and can make it unsafe. Direct model predictions were correct in 220/220 comparisons; the TTL dispatch rule was correct in 365/380, with 15 unsafe turns permitted and 0 safe turns rejected. These development measurements distinguish model errors from using a coarse expiry grid. The implementation is ready to measure an independent frozen dataset, but these results do not establish generalization or justify changing the predictor. No parameters were tuned.

## Overall accuracy

| Measurement | Tests | Accuracy | False-safe | False-rejection |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Raw prediction | 220 | 1.000 | 0 | 0 |
| TTL dispatch decision | 380 | 0.961 | 15 | 0 |

SAFE means at least 5 cm body clearance throughout the entire flight, including waiting and after checkpoint passage. Completion also requires reaching the fixed checkpoint at the required velocity for the required dwell before the deadline; it is context, not the prediction target. Readiness and recovery are outside this experiment.

These are grid-resolved observations, not exact threshold errors; unobserved thresholds are excluded rather than extrapolated.

## Computation performance

20 approval forecasts, one per scenario: mean 43.62 ms, median 42.92 ms, p95 56.45 ms, maximum 61.49 ms. The existing predictor measures elapsed call-to-result time, including model construction and all eleven delay rollouts. Its numerical kernels were warmed with one model control step before the measured forecasts; no extra approval forecast was run. Cold-start time and dispatch readiness are not measured here.

## Interpretation and next step

Observed: 15/15 TTL false-safe decisions occurred at delays the model did not evaluate. For example, in recorded seed 0, a 0.14 s wait produced 3.69 cm minimum body clearance, below the required 5 cm. The TTL rule still permitted that turn because its first predicted unsafe delay was 0.20 s. This establishes a gap in the existing TTL decisions; it does not establish what a direct model rollout at that untested delay would predict.

Raw accuracy applies only to directly evaluated delays. TTL accuracy also includes the gaps between them: an unsafe turn inside a gap can still be permitted until the next predicted unsafe grid point. Inspect the separate confusion matrices before attributing any error to the model. This experiment changes neither the 0.10 s prediction grid nor the expiry rule, and performs no recovery-policy comparison. Use the same frozen measurement procedure on independently calibrated evaluation scenarios; do not treat these 380 delay comparisons as 380 independent scenarios.

Technical note: the source flight journal stores violation time from flight start. This journal also retains that original value as first_violation_flight_s, and records first_violation_s relative to approval as required. Source and snapshot checks, cached forecasts, resumption state and this report are retained in run.json.

Validation: all 380 unique comparisons and 20 measured forecasts were verified. All confusion-matrix invariants and six focused TTL tests passed. Metrics reproduced exactly from the journal and fixed protocol without importing PyBullet. Resuming the completed run added no predictions or comparison records and preserved the journal and metrics byte-for-byte. Historical artifacts and scientific source files remain unchanged.
